VIDEO.title: God’s Wrath Is Already Happening (Romans 1)
VIDEO.series: The Book of Romans, Every Word (playlist of 28 videos)

kicker: Study aid · Romans 1:18-32 · Episode 3 (#3 of 28 in the playlist)
SUMMARY: The teacher reads Romans 1:18-32. The wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of people who suppress the truth. What can be known about God is evident to them through creation, so they are without excuse. Though they knew God, they did not glorify Him, exchanged His glory for images, and God gave them over: to impurity, to dishonorable passions, and to an unfit mind, ending in a long list of sins and approval of those who practice them.

'For' in verse 18 ties this passage to the theme in 1:16-17 by contrast. In 1:17 the righteousness of God is revealed and lived out by faith; in 1:18 His wrath is revealed, and the teacher argues it shows up the same way, in the way people live. Leon Morris (quoted in the video) defines wrath as the settled and active opposition of God's holy nature to everything that is evil. Without the bad news there is no good news.

'They knew God' (1:21) is relational knowledge. Who once knew God and then turned? The teacher hears Adam and Eve: not glorifying God, trusting their own wisdom (1:22), exchanging the truth for a lie (1:25). Eden is the template for all human sin, and the creature list in 1:23 echoes Genesis 1:26.
The threefold 'God gave them over' (1:24, 26, 28) traces a downward slope: sinful desire, then dishonorable passion, then a debased mind. The consequences of sin slope ever downward.

Connections: wrath in Deuteronomy 9:7-8, Isaiah 10:25; 30:27, Micah 7:9, Nahum 1:2, 6, Genesis 6:5-7, Deuteronomy 32:16-22 and Psalm 7:11; creation speaks in Psalm 19:1-6 and Job 12:7-10; exchanged glory in Psalm 106:20 (the golden calf) and Jeremiah 2:11; 'gave them over' in Psalm 81:12 and Judges 2:11-14.

'The truth of God' (1:25) is God's self-disclosed truth, and the Greek says 'the lie.' The lesson: from Eden to everyone, the essence of sin is the creation trying to be the creator, believing the lie that we can live as our own gods. That still entices believers, which is why Jesus calls us to deny ourselves daily (Luke 9:23).
QUOTES: From Eden to everyone, the essence of sin is the creation trying to be the creator, believing the lie that we can live as our own gods.
Paul is saying that in contrast to the Christian's lifestyle that reveals God's saving righteousness, the non-believer's wicked lifestyle reveals God's wrath.
He's using Adam and Eve's rebellion as a template for all human sin, showing that what happened in Eden happens again and again and again in every human heart.
The consequences of sin slope ever downward.

LSB_QUOTES.text: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men who suppress the truth in unrighteousness,

For since the creation of the world His invisible attributes, both His eternal power and divine nature, have been clearly seen, being understood through what has been made, so that they are without excuse.
For they exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen.

left.text: For in it the righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith; as it is written, “But the righteous will live by faith.”

right.text: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men who suppress the truth in unrighteousness,

lines.text: 'For' links verse 18 to the theme of 1:16-17. The righteousness of God is behind the gospel and its effect on a believer's life; the same righteousness stands behind His wrath, because the world's unrighteousness opposes Him.

How is wrath revealed? The teacher says: the same way, through lifestyle. Dishonored bodies (1:24), false worship (1:25), exchanged relations (1:26-27), every kind of unrighteousness (1:29-31), and approval of others who do the same (1:32). And they are without excuse (1:20).

left.text: God is a righteous judge, / And a God who has indignation every day. / If a man does not repent, He will sharpen His sword; / He has bent His bow and prepared it.

right.text: Who can stand before His indignation? / Who can endure the burning of His anger? / His wrath is poured out like fire, / And the rocks are torn down by Him.

lines.text: Wrath is explicit in Deuteronomy 9:7-8, Isaiah 10:25; 30:27, Micah 7:9 and Nahum 1:2, 6, and implicit in God's actions against wickedness in Genesis 6:5-7 and Deuteronomy 32:16-22. Psalm 7 makes Paul's link: God's wrath flows from His righteousness.
Leon Morris, quoted in the video: wrath is the settled and active opposition of God's holy nature to everything that is evil. It is not a temper; it is righteousness meeting evil.

left.text: For the choir director. A Psalm of David. / The heavens are telling of the glory of God; / And the expanse is declaring the work of His hands. / Day to day pours forth speech, / And night to night reveals knowledge.

right.text: “Who among all these does not know / That the hand of Yahweh has done this, / In whose hand is the life of every living thing, / And the breath of all the flesh of man?

lines.text: 'That which is known about God is evident within them; for God made it evident to them' (Romans 1:19). Days and nights speak of the Lord in a voice everyone hears (Psalm 19:2-6), and the beasts, birds and fish testify that 'the hand of Yahweh has done this' (Job 12:9).
Study note (added): Paul makes the same appeal to pagan audiences: God 'did not leave Himself without witness' (Acts 14:17), and 'He is not far from each one of us' (Acts 17:27).

left.text: For even though they knew God, they did not glorify Him as God or give thanks, but they became futile in their thoughts, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing to be wise, they became fools,

right.text: Then the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes, and that the tree was desirable to make one wise, so she took from its fruit and ate; and she gave also to her husband with her, and he ate.

lines.text: This knowledge is relational, not just intellectual. How could people who reject God once have known Him? The teacher hears Adam and Eve: they knew God, did not honor Him, reached for wisdom on their own terms, and believed the serpent's lie, 'you will be like God' (Genesis 3:5).
Paul uses Eden as an archetype: every person's sin echoes the first sin, choosing our own way over God's way.

left.text: and exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for an image in the likeness of corruptible man and of birds and four-footed animals and crawling creatures.

right.text: Then God said, “Let Us make man in Our image, according to Our likeness, so that they will have dominion over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the sky and over the cattle and over all the earth and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth.”

lines.text: The list of creatures in 1:23 comes from Genesis 1. Humans made to rule creation as God's image bow down to images of the very creatures they were to rule. Another sign that Paul has creation and the fall in mind.
Study note (added): Deuteronomy 4:15-18 forbids images in the likeness of male or female, animal, bird, creeping thing or fish, the same categories.

left.text: They made a calf in Horeb / And worshiped a molten image. / Thus they exchanged their glory / For the image of an ox that eats grass.

right.text: Has a nation changed gods / Though they were not gods? / But My people have changed their glory / For that which does not profit.

lines.text: Psalm 106 remembers Aaron and Israel making the golden calf (Exodus 32). The same verb idea, 'exchanged,' runs through Romans 1:23, 25 and 26. Israel did it too, which Paul will press in chapters 2 and 3.

GIVEN.title: God gave them over, three times

src.text: And just as they did not see fit to acknowledge God, God gave them over to an unfit mind, to do those things which are not proper,

lines.text: 'God gave them over in the lusts of their hearts' (1:24); 'God gave them over to dishonorable passions' (1:26); 'God gave them over to an unfit mind' (1:28). Desire becomes passion, and passion becomes debased reasoning.
Those who reject God for moral autonomy can count on this path as the Lord hands them over to their own ways. The more one partakes, the easier the descent.

left.text: “But My people did not listen to My voice, / And Israel was not willing to obey Me. / “So I released them over to the stubbornness of their heart, / That they would walk in their own devices.

right.text: And the anger of Yahweh burned against Israel, and He gave them into the hands of plunderers who plundered them; and He sold them into the hands of their enemies around them, so that they could no longer stand before their enemies.

lines.text: In Judges 2, Israel served the Baals and the Ashtaroth and forsook Yahweh; His anger burned and He gave them over. Wrath that hands people over to their own ways is where Paul is drawing from.

GIVEN.title: The truth of God and the lie

src.text: For they exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen.

lines.text: The video's translation reads 'the truth about God,' but the Greek genitive is better read 'the truth of God,' as the LSB has it. Context decides: verses 19-21 speak of what God made evident about Himself. This is not man's truth about God; it is the truth that comes from God and concerns who He is.
And the Greek says 'the lie,' not just 'a lie.' The lesson follows: from Eden to everyone, sin is the creature trying to be the Creator.

BACKGROUND.p: Jewish writings of Paul's era, such as the Wisdom of Solomon (chapters 13-14), argued that pagans should have known the Creator from creation and that idolatry leads to immorality. Paul's readers would have recognized the pattern, and in Romans 2 he turns it on the one who agrees.
Rome and Corinth were full of temples and statues of gods, emperors, animals and heroes. 'An image in the likeness of corruptible man' described the street outside.
Lists of vices were common in Greek moral writing and in Jewish teaching. Paul's list (1:29-31) moves from inner attitudes to social sins and ends with 'disobedient to parents' and 'unmerciful.'

Paul names exchanged sexual relations as one example of the exchange of the Creator for the creature, alongside envy, gossip and arrogance. The video treats it as one item in the list, not a special category; Paul's next move (2:1) warns the reader who judges others.

DEBATES.p: The video: through the lifestyle of those God gives over, a present wrath. Others stress future judgment announced in the gospel (2:5), or both: present handing over now, final judgment later.
Many hear Adam and Eve behind 1:21-25, as the video does; others see mainly Israel's golden calf (Psalm 106:20) or Gentile idolatry in general. The echoes can work together.
The video: all Gentiles, with Adam as the archetype, and then Israel too in chapters 2-3. Romans 3:23 gathers everyone: 'all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.'

CAREFUL_INTRO: Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
CAREFUL: In 1:25 the video's translation has truth 'about' God; the LSB already reads 'the truth of God,' though 'a lie' rather than 'the lie.'

The video calls the Greek 'to' a genitive article; it is tou, and the of/about question turns on the genitive noun phrase as a whole. The conclusion (God's self-disclosed truth) is a reasonable reading.
The video cites Psalm 7:11 but reads on into 7:12 ('If a man does not repent...').
The captions say 'Romans chapter 2 verse 11 of Judges'; the passage read is Judges 2:11-14.
Romans 1:17 says the righteousness of God is revealed 'in it,' that is, in the gospel. That believers' lives display it is the video's application, not Paul's wording.

QUESTIONS: How does seeing 1:18 as the contrast to 1:17 change how you read this hard passage?
Where do you see creation 'telling of the glory of God' in your own life?
What does it mean that God's wrath can look like Him handing people over to what they want?
In what small ways do you still try to be your own god?
How does Jesus' call to deny yourself daily answer the Eden pattern?
APPLICATION_VIDEO: From Eden to everyone, the essence of sin is the creation trying to be the creator, believing the lie that we can live as our own gods. All sin shares the same fruit-stealing quality. This is not only about Gentiles; Paul will turn to Israel in chapters 2 and 3 to show that all have sinned (Romans 3:23). It still entices believers: Jesus told His followers to deny themselves and take up their cross daily (Luke 9:23), which assumes an ongoing struggle with the self. The self has been dealt with on the cross, even if it still whispers. As Miles Stanford put it (quoted in the video), our Father takes us down until the self life is uncovered, and then up as the Christ life is discovered.
APPLICATION_ADDED: Study note (added): spend ten minutes outside this week and read Psalm 19:1-6 there. Then name one 'exchange' you are tempted to make, and pray Luke 9:23 over it.

Days and nights speak of the Lord in a voice everyone hears (Psalm 19:2-6), and the beasts, birds and fish testify that 'the hand of Yahweh has done this' (Job 12:9). (Psalm 19:2-6; Job 12:7-8)
   [Background] Study note (added): Paul makes the same appeal to pagan audiences: God 'did not leave Himself without witness' (Acts 14:17), and 'He is not far from each one of us' (Acts 17:27). (Acts 14:15-17; Acts 17:24-29)

## The Eden template
1. Romans 1:21-22; Genesis 3:5-6: They knew God
   Paul (Romans 1:21-22, LSB): "For even though they knew God, they did not glorify Him as God or give thanks, but they became futile in their thoughts, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing to be wise, they became fools,"
   Moses (Genesis 3:6, LSB): "Then the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes, and that the tree was desirable to make one wise, so she took from its fruit and ate; and she gave also to her husband with her, and he ate."
   (video) This knowledge is relational, not just intellectual. How could people who reject God once have known Him? The teacher hears Adam and Eve: they knew God, did not honor Him, reached for wisdom on their own terms, and believed the serpent's lie, 'you will be like God' (Genesis 3:5). (Genesis 3:5)
   (video) Paul uses Eden as an archetype: every person's sin echoes the first sin, choosing our own way over God's way.
2. Romans 1:23; Genesis 1:26: Birds, animals, creeping things
   Paul (Romans 1:23, LSB): "and exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for an image in the likeness of corruptible man and of birds and four-footed animals and crawling creatures."
   Moses (Genesis 1:26, LSB): "Then God said, “Let Us make man in Our image, according to Our likeness, so that they will have dominion over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the sky and over the cattle and over all the earth and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth.”"
   (video) The list of creatures in 1:23 comes from Genesis 1. Humans made to rule creation as God's image bow down to images of the very creatures they were to rule. Another sign that Paul has creation and the fall in mind.
   [Background] Study note (added): Deuteronomy 4:15-18 forbids images in the likeness of male or female, animal, bird, creeping thing or fish, the same categories. (Deuteronomy 4:15-18)
3. Psalm 106:20; Jeremiah 2:11: They exchanged their glory
   Psalmist (Psalm 106:19-20, LSB): "They made a calf in Horeb / And worshiped a molten image. / Thus they exchanged their glory / For the image of an ox that eats grass."
   Jeremiah (Jeremiah 2:11, LSB): "Has a nation changed gods / Though they were not gods? / But My people have changed their glory / For that which does not profit."
   (video) Psalm 106 remembers Aaron and Israel making the golden calf (Exodus 32). The same verb idea, 'exchanged,' runs through Romans 1:23, 25 and 26. Israel did it too, which Paul will press in chapters 2 and 3. (Exodus 32:4)

## God gave them over
1. Romans 1:24, 26, 28: God gave them over, three times
   The downward slope Romans 1:28: "And just as they did not see fit to acknowledge God, God gave them over to an unfit mind, to do those things which are not proper," https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Romans+1:28
   (video) 'God gave them over in the lusts of their hearts' (1:24); 'God gave them over to dishonorable passions' (1:26); 'God gave them over to an unfit mind' (1:28). Desire becomes passion, and passion becomes debased reasoning.
   (video) Those who reject God for moral autonomy can count on this path as the Lord hands them over to their own ways. The more one partakes, the easier the descent.
2. Psalm 81:11-12; Judges 2:12-14: Released to their own devices
   Asaph (Psalm 81:11-12, LSB): "“But My people did not listen to My voice, / And Israel was not willing to obey Me. / “So I released them over to the stubbornness of their heart, / That they would walk in their own devices."
   Judges (Judges 2:14, LSB): "And the anger of Yahweh burned against Israel, and He gave them into the hands of plunderers who plundered them; and He sold them into the hands of their enemies around them, so that they could no longer stand before their enemies."
   (video) In Judges 2, Israel served the Baals and the Ashtaroth and forsook Yahweh; His anger burned and He gave them over. Wrath that hands people over to their own ways is where Paul is drawing from. (Judges 2:11-13)
3. Romans 1:25: The truth of God and the lie
   Self-disclosed truth Romans 1:25: "For they exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen." https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Romans+1:25
   (video) The video's translation reads 'the truth about God,' but the Greek genitive is better read 'the truth of God,' as the LSB has it. Context decides: verses 19-21 speak of what God made evident about Himself. This is not man's truth about God; it is the truth that comes from God and concerns who He is.
   (video) And the Greek says 'the lie,' not just 'a lie.' The lesson follows: from Eden to everyone, sin is the creature trying to be the Creator.

## Key people
- Adam and Eve: The template for all human sin: they knew God, then did not honor Him. [Background] Paul makes Adam explicit later (Romans 5:12-21).
- Aaron and Israel: Psalm 106 recalls the golden calf: they exchanged their glory. [Background] Exodus 32; even God's people exchanged His glory for an image.
- David: Psalm 7: a righteous judge; Psalm 19: the heavens tell of God's glory. [Background] Both psalms carry headings naming David.
- Job: 'Ask the beasts': creation testifies to its Maker. [Background] Job speaks these words in his reply to his friends.
- Leon Morris: Quoted for his definition of God's wrath. [Background] An Australian New Testament scholar who wrote a Romans commentary; the video does not name the book.
- Miles Stanford: Quoted on the self life and the Christ life. [Background] A twentieth-century Christian writer on the believer's growth; the video does not name the book.

## Places [Background]
- Rome: The church that reads this letter.
- Corinth: Where Paul writes, in a city of many temples.
- Mount Sinai (traditional) (named in the video): Horeb, where Israel made the calf (Psalm 106:19). Traditional site; the location is debated.
- Egypt (named in the video): God their Savior 'had done great things in Egypt' (Psalm 106:21).
- Athens: Paul on idols: the Divine Nature is not like gold or silver or stone (Acts 17:29).
- Lystra: 'He did not leave Himself without witness' (Acts 14:17).

## Key terms
- Wrath of God: In Leon Morris's words (quoted in the video), the settled and active opposition of God's holy nature to everything that is evil.
- Suppress the truth: To hold down what one knows; they 'suppress the truth in unrighteousness' (Romans 1:18).
- Without excuse: No defense: God's 'eternal power and divine nature, have been clearly seen' (Romans 1:20).
- Gave them over: Handed them over to their own choices; three times in 1:24, 26, 28 (compare Psalm 81:12).
- The truth of God: The truth God has disclosed about Himself, exchanged for 'the lie' (Romans 1:25).
- Idolatry: Worshiping and serving the creature rather than the Creator (Romans 1:25). [Background]

## Hebrew and Greek words [Background; Strong's numbers follow the LSB's word tagging]
- ὀργή orgē (G3709, Greek): Anger, wrath; settled indignation, often of God's judgment. Look up: BDAG, ὀργή. (Rom 1:18)
- κατέχω katechō (G2722, Greek): To hold fast; to hold back, suppress. (Rom 1:18)
- ἀναπολόγητος anapologētos (G379, Greek): Without excuse, without a defense. (Rom 1:20)
- ἀλλάσσω allassō (G236, Greek): To change, exchange. (Rom 1:23)
- παραδίδωμι paradidōmi (G3860, Greek): To hand over, give over, deliver up. Look up: BDAG, παραδίδωμι. (Rom 1:24, 26, 28)
- ψεῦδος pseudos (G5579, Greek): Lie, falsehood. (Rom 1:25)
- ἀδόκιμος adokimos (G96, Greek): Failing the test, unfit, worthless; 'an unfit mind' after they did not 'see fit' to acknowledge God. (Rom 1:28)
- כָּבוֹד kavod (H3519, Hebrew): Weight, honor, glory. Look up: HALOT or BDB, כָּבוֹד. (Ps 106:20; Jer 2:11)

## Historical and cultural background [Background: established]
- Jewish arguments against idols: Jewish writings of Paul's era, such as the Wisdom of Solomon (chapters 13-14), argued that pagans should have known the Creator from creation and that idolatry leads to immorality. Paul's readers would have recognized the pattern, and in Romans 2 he turns it on the one who agrees.
- A city full of images: Rome and Corinth were full of temples and statues of gods, emperors, animals and heroes. 'An image in the likeness of corruptible man' described the street outside.
- Vice lists: Lists of vices were common in Greek moral writing and in Jewish teaching. Paul's list (1:29-31) moves from inner attitudes to social sins and ends with 'disobedient to parents' and 'unmerciful.'
- 1:26-27: Paul names exchanged sexual relations as one example of the exchange of the Creator for the creature, alongside envy, gossip and arrogance. The video treats it as one item in the list, not a special category; Paul's next move (2:1) warns the reader who judges others.

## Where scholars differ [Background: debated]
- How is wrath 'revealed' (1:18)? The video: through the lifestyle of those God gives over, a present wrath. Others stress future judgment announced in the gospel (2:5), or both: present handing over now, final judgment later.
- Adam in Romans 1? Many hear Adam and Eve behind 1:21-25, as the video does; others see mainly Israel's golden calf (Psalm 106:20) or Gentile idolatry in general. The echoes can work together.
- Who is described? The video: all Gentiles, with Adam as the archetype, and then Israel too in chapters 2-3. Romans 3:23 gathers everyone: 'all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.'

## Careful reading notes
Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
- In 1:25 the video's translation has truth 'about' God; the LSB already reads 'the truth of God,' though 'a lie' rather than 'the lie.'
- The video calls the Greek 'to' a genitive article; it is tou, and the of/about question turns on the genitive noun phrase as a whole. The conclusion (God's self-disclosed truth) is a reasonable reading.
- The video cites Psalm 7:11 but reads on into 7:12 ('If a man does not repent...').
- The captions say 'Romans chapter 2 verse 11 of Judges'; the passage read is Judges 2:11-14.
- Romans 1:17 says the righteousness of God is revealed 'in it,' that is, in the gospel. That believers' lives display it is the video's application, not Paul's wording.

## Reflection and discussion questions
1. How does seeing 1:18 as the contrast to 1:17 change how you read this hard passage?
2. Where do you see creation 'telling of the glory of God' in your own life?
3. What does it mean that God's wrath can look like Him handing people over to what they want?
4. In what small ways do you still try to be your own god?
5. How does Jesus' call to deny yourself daily answer the Eden pattern?

## Application
- (video) From Eden to everyone, the essence of sin is the creation trying to be the creator, believing the lie that we can live as our own gods. All sin shares the same fruit-stealing quality. This is not only about Gentiles; Paul will turn to Israel in chapters 2 and 3 to show that all have sinned (Romans 3:23). It still entices believers: Jesus told His followers to deny themselves and take up their cross daily (Luke 9:23), which assumes an ongoing struggle with the self. The self has been dealt with on the cross, even if it still whispers. As Miles Stanford put it (quoted in the video), our Father takes us down until the self life is uncovered, and then up as the Christ life is discovered.
- Study note (added): spend ten minutes outside this week and read Psalm 19:1-6 there. Then name one 'exchange' you are tempted to make, and pray Luke 9:23 over it.
